name: Ahmad Osman
bio:
Ahmad M. Osman is an AI researcher, systems engineer, and moderator of r/LocalLLaMA, where he helps a fast-growing community make local AI practical. A lifelong builder, he started coding at age 7, and by age 12 was running a private C++ MMORPG server from a Pentium 4 desktop.

Today, Ahmad’s work sits at the intersection of LLMs, inference, hardware, infrastructure, and full-stack ownership. He holds dual degrees in Computer Science and Data Science, and is a prominent voice in modern AI infrastructure and self-hosted artificial intelligence.

When not on stage, Ahmad can be found building Osmantic, his sovereign AI lab, where he serves as Founder and CEO.

positions.claim: Within roughly 18 months (late 2027), GLM 5.2-class intelligence will run on a single RTX 5090 with 32GB of VRAM.
A capability gap between frontier and open-source models will always exist, but it will keep shrinking.
Capability density follows a 'densing law' of roughly 50% fewer parameters for equivalent capability every 3.5 months.
The trend is not small models beating big models, but newer efficient models beating older inefficient ones — driven by compounding research, not chance.
A 27B dense model (Qwen 3.6) now beats Llama 405B, an inversion that took under two years (summer 2024 to March 2026, ~21 months).
GLM 5.2 beats GPT-5.5 extra-high on at least one benchmark.
NVFP4 training (demonstrated by Nemotron 3 Ultra) makes fine-tuning and specialized model creation cheaper and economically viable sooner.
Open-source AI cannot win unless enterprises move off cloud subsidies and own their hardware stack end to end.
Cloud token prices are currently subsidized and those subsidies will go away, leaving subscribers with limitations.
GPUs purchased today become more valuable over time as models get more efficient — the RTX 3090, a 2020 architecture, still sells above MSRP.
You should buy a GPU rather than rent cloud inference.
Post-training improvements on the same checkpoint can deliver large capability gains without new pretraining.
